source_message.text:
Yes, that's correct. The main board has:

\- ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 module
\- INA219 current monitor (on the 3.3V rail)
\- USB-C connector (programming port) + LDO for standalone operation
\- All the JST connectors (to power board, sensor board, display, PIR, touch, LEDs, buttons, reset)
\- Support passives: decoupling caps, pull-ups, series resistors, Schottky diodes, BOOT button

No sensors, no power management — those are on the other boards.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: regarding power metering: I need to measure the 5V rail current as well — the SPS30, ZE08 and LEDs are the heaviest consumers so it's actually more important than the 3.3V rail. The only way I knew how to do it was adding a second INA219 at address 0x41, but wanted to ask if you have a better idea?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The three boards are chained: power board → main board → sensor board. The main board is in the middle, so power enters from the power board (J\_PWR\_PWR) and the main board uses it locally AND forwards it to the sensor board (J\_SENSOR\_PWR). Think of it like a power strip — power comes in one cable, and the main board distributes it both to its own components and passes it along to the sensor board via a second cable.
The INA219 sits in-series on the 3.3V rail right after the Schottky diodes — so it measures the total 3.3V current for everything downstream: the ESP32 itself, plus whatever the sensor board draws, all in one reading.
